audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Frost Armor grants immunity to slows — in a matchup whose entire plan is 'point-and-click Wither her'. spikes[0] actively tells you to Wither her at the exact moment she has Frost Armor up.
audit.why: Fury of the North: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows.' Wither is a slow. spikes[0] currently reads 'point-and-click it onto Sejuani the instant she Frost-armor walks up' — that is precisely when the movement slow will not stick. Since Frost Armor only 'persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage', the correct play is to land damage first to break it, then spend Wither. This is the single decisive interaction in the lane and the current text has it exactly backwards.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor makes her immune to slows. Break it with damage before you spend Wither, or the movement slow is wasted.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Sejuani combo order is reversed everywhere. spikes[1] 'a Q or E auto-proc into Winter's Wrath (W)', wants.foe[0] 'Land Permafrost (E stun) off an auto/Q proc to lock you for a Winter's Wrath', mid 'E-stun into a W shove', whys[3] 'an E stun into W shove'.
audit.why: Permafrost 'freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks' — it is a finisher that requires the stacks to already be there. Winter's Wrath is the ability whose text says it applies Frost stacks. So the sequence is W first, E second; Permafrost cannot open. A player watching for the stun as the opening move will misread every engage she makes, and will not learn that Winter's Wrath is the tell.
audit.corrected: Winter's Wrath applies the Frost stacks; Permafrost only stuns once they are maxed. Watch the W, not the E.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is keyed to 'track Permafrost's cooldown' — breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, loading ('Engage only on Permafrost's cooldown'), dosFull[0], dosFull[2], winCon.
audit.why: Permafrost's cooldown is 1.5 seconds. There is no window to track and no way to engage 'on its cooldown' — the advice cannot be executed. The genuine gate is her Frost stack count, and the genuine long cooldown in her kit is Arctic Assault at 18s at rank 1, which is her only engage and is never mentioned anywhere.
audit.corrected: Track Frost stacks, not Permafrost's 1.5s cooldown. Arctic Assault at 18s at rank 1 is the real engage cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[3] call Winter's Wrath a 'percent-HP shove', while the same file's 'late' says she 'has no true damage or percent-HP burst to race my HP bar'.
audit.why: The file contradicts itself, and the kit sides with 'late': Sejuani's derived kitFlags contain no percentHealth entry at all, and Winter's Wrath's text is 'dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks' with no max-health component described. Telling a Nasus that a tank has percent-health damage changes his itemisation — he will buy resistances differently — so this is not cosmetic.
audit.corrected: Drop the 'percent-HP' descriptor from Winter's Wrath; describe it as the Frost applier.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (W text; kitFlags has no percentHealth)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] and 'late' call Glacial Prison an 'AOE stun'.
audit.why: Glacial Prison 'throws her bola that freezes and stuns the first champion hit and creates an ice storm that slows other enemies.' Only the first champion hit is stunned; everyone else is slowed. Calling it an AoE stun overstates what it does to a grouped team and, more importantly for the advice given, misrepresents what happens when Nasus splitpushes into it.
audit.corrected: Glacial Prison is a line bola that stuns only the first champion it hits; the rest are slowed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two full-layer fields refer to Sejuani as male: dosFull[2].t 'Wither him the moment Permafrost is down' and dontsFull[0].t 'Fight his Permafrost window'.
audit.why: Straight copy artefacts from a templated male-pronoun entry. Both are user-facing strings.

At 3 my Wither flips it — point-and-click slow her the second she steps up and she can't follow up the stun.
edits.after: Neither of us does anything level 1-2 — Sejuani has no poke and I'm just soaking Q farm, so stack freely and don't get greedy on a cannon. Learn her order: Winter's Wrath (W) is what applies Frost stacks, and Permafrost (E) only stuns once they are maxed, so the W is the tell, not the E. Her engage is Arctic Assault (Q), an 18-second charge at rank 1, and it is the only way she closes on you. Respect that her CC, not her damage, is what hurts you.

notes: SCOPE LIMIT I deliberately did not cross, please verify before trusting it further: Riot's text says Frost Armor grants 'immunity to slows', which I have applied only to Wither's movement-speed component. Whether that immunity also suppresses Wither's attack-speed reduction is not answerable from the kit files — in League those are usually treated as separate debuff categories — so every edit above says 'the movement half' or just 'the slow' and none of them claims her attack speed is protected. Worth a League Wiki check on Fury of the North's exact immunity scope; if it does cover attack speed too, the level-6 window in this entry needs rethinking entirely. Second caveat on the same passive: Frost Armor 'persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage', so 'break it with damage' is not instant — there is a brief grace period I have not tried to quantify. Finally, this matchup came through the packet with ZERO flagged defects and turned out to contain the worst interaction error in my slice, because the defect detector only looks for missing or misspelled ability names and every name here was already spelled correctly. Name-presence is not a proxy for mechanical correctness.
